# Laplace HypoPINN

> Laplace HypoPINN is a Python/PyTorch research package for two-dimensional seismic hypocenter localization using physics-informed neural networks and local Laplace approximations of network-weight uncertainty.

The package learns travel-time fields from a velocity model and receiver travel times, then estimates sources from field minima. Its functional API supports configurable and custom pointwise models. Install from the GitHub checkout using Python 3.12 or later; the smoke example and tutorials run on CPU.

## Documentation

- [Overview and installation](https://izzatum.github.io/laplace-hypopinn/): Project scope, clone/install commands and research workflow.
- [Tutorials](https://izzatum.github.io/laplace-hypopinn/tutorials/): Eight executed notebooks covering historical diagonal, GGN diagonal, block diagonal, full GGN, KFAC, EFB, INF and VaLLA.
- [Method definitions](https://izzatum.github.io/laplace-hypopinn/methods/): Residual weighting, curvature equations, damping, method sources and predictive conventions.
- [Architecture](https://izzatum.github.io/laplace-hypopinn/architecture/): Functional API, custom models, data contracts, random state and saved artifacts.
- [Reproducibility](https://izzatum.github.io/laplace-hypopinn/reproducibility/): Historical presets, coordinates, notebook/paper differences and evidence needed for comparison claims.
- [Performance and validation](https://izzatum.github.io/laplace-hypopinn/performance/): Recorded CPU measurements, reference comparisons and scaling limits.
- [FAQ](https://izzatum.github.io/laplace-hypopinn/faq/): Direct answers about installation, methods, custom models, data, uncertainty and licensing.
- [Citation](https://izzatum.github.io/laplace-hypopinn/citation/): Full paper reference and BibTeX for Izzatullah, Yildirim, Waheed and Alkhalifah (2022), DOI 10.1088/2632-2153/ac94b3.

## Interpretation

Reported uncertainty is local variation induced by neural-network weights; it does not alone establish calibrated source-location, velocity or arrival-pick uncertainty. Teaching notebooks use reduced budgets. Positive posterior regularization is post-hoc damping unless training used the matching prior and likelihood scale. VaLLA uses linearized predictions; the other methods use nonlinear evaluation at sampled weights. Historical diagonal curvature differs from the maintained GGN target.

This file is an optional documentation index. It does not replace the linked method definitions, numerical evidence or license terms.
